title: Social engineering in practice
intro: Spot tricks in calls, texts and visits. Decide what you would do in each moment from this module's lessons.

decisions.title: Call from SahilBank

artifact.name: SahilBank
body: Hello, this is Fuad Mammadov from SahilBank security. Someone is trying to take 1,200 manat from your card right now.

options.label: I give the last card digits
I share no card details by phone

decisions.explain: Never give card details on an incoming call; the name and number can be faked.

decisions.title: Message from +44 7700 900456
decisions.prompt: The number is new, the name is familiar. What do you do with this message?

body: Hi Mum! It's me, Aysel. My phone broke, this is my new number.

decisions.explain: A new number with a familiar name is checked through another channel, such as the old number.

decisions.title: Message from IT Support (new)
decisions.prompt: An unknown technician, and no pass. What do you do with this message?

artifact.name: IT Support (new)
body: Hi, I have come to fix your printer and I am at the entrance. I left my pass at home, can you come down and open the door?

options.label: I call the official IT support number

decisions.explain: Check an unexpected technician's visit yourself through the official channel.

decisions.title: Call: SahilBank

artifact.name: Call: SahilBank
body: We saw a suspicious payment on your card. Do not tell us anything, call the number on the back of your card.

decisions.explain: It asks for nothing and sends you to the official number. Call the number on your card to check.

decisions.title: Call: +994 12 000 11 22

artifact.name: Call: +994 12 000 11 22
body: This is the police. A loan was opened in your name. Move your money to a safe account now.

decisions.explain: The police never ask you to move money to a safe account. This is a well known scam.
